verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Floating in the Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego" (R1); "splashdown... off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashdown off the coast of San Diego" (R3, R4, R6); "off San Diego" (R5); "off the coast of San Diego, California" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All references directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Friday... 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" (R1); "8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R2); "Friday night... 8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT" (R3, R4); "7:07 p.m. CST Friday" [equiv. to 8:07 EDT] (R5); "8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT... April 10, 2026" (R6); "April 10, 2026... 8:07 p.m. ET" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the exact date, day, and time in EDT/PDT.

verifications.claim: The crew consisted of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" (R1); "The Artemis II crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA... Jeremy Hansen" (R2); "the four astronauts" (R3); "four-person crew" (R4); "four astronauts" (R5); "crew of four astronauts" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant references explicitly state or list exactly four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The crew successfully completed a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "journey around the moon... April 1... Friday [April 10]" [~10 days] (R1); "694,481-mile journey... lunar flyby" (R2); "10 days... mission to the Moon... flyby" (R3); "10 days... lunar flyby mission" (R4); "nearly 10-day mission around the Moon" (R5); "historic 10-day mission to the moon" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: References confirm ~10-day duration, lunar flyby/mission around the moon, and success.

verifications.claim: The crew was retrieved by US Navy divers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "recovery team... helped the astronauts out" [Navy context] (R1); "U.S. military recovery team... Recovery teams will retrieve the crew" (R2); "retrieved by US Navy divers" (R4); "Navy divers... divers will open the hatch" (R5); "U.S. Navy sailors on a dive... divers were there to open the capsule" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly mention US Navy divers retrieving or assisting crew extraction.

verifications.claim: The crew was transported via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "hoisted them up for hovering helicopters to take them to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha" (R1); "fly them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "flown via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha" (R3); "delivered via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha" (R4); "individually airlifted to the USS John P. Murtha" (R5); "hoisted into a helicopter... to the ship" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm helicopter transport to USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972" (R1); "first humans toward the Moon since 1972" (R2); "NASA’s first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years" (R3); "first astronauts to journey around the moon in more than 50 years" (R4); "NASA’s first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly describe it as the first crewed Artemis mission since Apollo era.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was designed as a test flight before future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "demonstrated that their Orion spacecraft can handle... sets up the next steps... moon in 2028" (R1); "evaluated Orion’s systems... tests" (R2); "test flight" (R3); "primarily serves as a test flight... ahead of a future moon landing" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: References directly state it as a test flight for Orion/systems ahead of lunar landings.

verifications.claim: Florida Today reported that this marked the successful conclusion of the 694,481-mile journey around the moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "completing the Artemis II crew’s return to Earth and a 694,481-mile journey" (R7, Florida Today); same phrasing in R2, R6 timelines
verifications.reasoning: R7 (Florida Today) mentions 694,481-mile journey in splashdown context implying completion, but not explicitly 'successful conclusion'; other sources confirm success and similar mileage but vary slightly (e.g., 700,237 miles).

verifications.claim: According to the official NASA blog, the crew is now undergoing post-mission medical evaluations.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Once aboard, the astronauts will undergo post‑mission medical evaluations" (R2, NASA blog)
verifications.reasoning: R2 (NASA blog) states they 'will undergo' post-mission evaluations (pre-splashdown tense), matching concept but not exact present tense 'is now undergoing'; other sources confirm it occurred.
